Text:
Tyra: PREVIOUSLY ON
"AMERICA'S NEXT TOP MODEL"...

SHANDI STRUGGLED TO LEAVE
HER PAST AS A CLERK
AT WALGREENS BEHIND...

Shandi: I'M GOING TO DO
ANYTHING TO CHANGE MY LIFE.

Camille: WHAT ARE YOU
HEARING?
Yoanna: I DON'T TRUST YOU.

Tyra: WHILE CAMILLE SPARKED
TENSIONS WITH HER COMPETITORS,

AND SARA DISOBEYED
HER FATHER'S WISHES.

Sara: HE CONSIDERS
MODELING PROSTITUTION.

Tyra: MERCEDES KEPT
HER ILLNESS A SECRET
FROM EVERYONE.

AND IN THE LAST ELIMINATION,
JENASCIA WAS SENT HOME.
EIGHT GIRLS REMAIN.
WHO WILL BE ELIMINATED TONIGHT?

Catie: THE PAST ELIMINATIONS
I'M FEELING RELIEVED.

I'M FEELING DISAPPOINTED
THAT I LET MYSELF SLIP
DOWN THE RANKINGS.

I JUST REALIZED THAT I REALLY
NEED TO UP MY GAME.

Camille: I MEAN, THEY CAN
CHOOSE, LIKE, A MILLION

BLONDE-HAIRED, BLUE-EYED GIRLS
TO WALK DOWN A RUNWAY,

BUT BLACK WOMEN IN A SHOW
ARE FAR AND FEW BETWEEN, OKAY?
IT'S VERY COMPETITIVE.
IT'S, LIKE, THAT ONE TOKEN GIRL.
April: WELL, COME ON.

WHAT PERCENTAGE
OF MAGAZINE COVERS
DO YOU SEE AN ASIAN ON?

IT'S ROUGHER BEING AN ASIAN
THAN A BLACK WOMAN.
TYRA'S TOLD ME RIGHT UP FRONT.

Tyra: THE FASHION INDUSTRY
IS ALL ABOUT RACE.
April: REALLY?

Tyra: DO YOU SEE ASIAN GIRLS
ON THE COVERS OF MAGAZINES?

AND I'M NOT TALKING
ABOUT LUCY LIU.
SHE'S AN ACTRESS.

SO YOU ENTERING
THIS FASHION WORLD--
YOU WOULD BE AN UNDERDOG.

April: BEFORE I DECIDED
TO ENTER INTO THIS INDUSTRY,

I NEVER REALLY THOUGHT
ABOUT MY ETHNICITY.

SHE SAID, "THERE'S LESS SLOTS
FOR YOU IN ANY RUNWAY SHOW,

EDITORIAL OF FASHION MAGAZINES
THAN ANY SINGLE OTHER RACE

YOU CAN EVEN THINK OF
RIGHT NOW."

I'M HALF JAPANESE,
AND I'M HALF CAUCASIAN,

BUT I'VE NEVER DONE ANYTHING
THAT MADE ME ASSOCIATE MYSELF
AS AN ASIAN.

Camille: I DON'T KNOW
HOW MUCH APRIL LIVES OUT

HER JAPANESE CULTURE
IN HER LIFE,

BUT HER JAPANESE HERITAGE
MIGHT BE THAT ONE THING
THAT'S GONNA GIVE HER THE EDGE.

Mercedes: THAT'S NICE--
LET ME SEE.
WHAT IS THAT?
Sara: IT'S FROM IRAN.
MOSQUES. IT'S HAND-PAINTED.

I AM SO PROUD
OF MY PERSIAN CULTURE,

BUT TO MY IRANIAN FAMILY--
MY FATHER, WHO'S MUSLIM,
A MODEL IS A WHORE.

Mercedes: I GOTTA
DO SOMETHING.

I WAS DIAGNOSED WITH LUPUS,
WHICH IS A CHRONIC ILLNESS THAT

ATTACKS YOUR IMMUNE SYSTEM,
ABOUT A YEAR AGO,

AND I DON'T WANT MY ROOMMATES
TO KNOW.
I HIDE EVERYTHING.

I TAKE PILLS UNDER THE COUNTER,
AND, LIKE, HURRY UP
AND DRINK SOME WATER.
I DON'T WANNA BE JUDGED.

I JUST WANNA BE AS NORMAL
AS EVERYBODY ELSE.
Tyra: HELLO.
LOOK AT YOU.
WHAT YOU DOIN'?
OKAY, COME ON.
WHOO! WHOO!
I CAN'T GET OUT.
AAH!
(laughter)
Tyra: NOW I'M ALL HOT.
OH, MY GOSH. COME OVER HERE.
OKAY.

YEAH, WE NEED TO GET
YOU GUYS SOME DOUBLE DUTCH.
Mercedes: YEAH.
Tyra: OKAY.
SO I'M REALLY PROUD OF YOU ALL.
YOU GUYS ARE REALLY STRONG.

FROM NOW ON,
IT'S GONNA BE REALLY DIFFICULT

WITH THE ELIMINATIONS,
AND I CAN TELL AFTER JUDGING

HOW HEAVY THE WHOLE EXPERIENCE
OF THIS COMPETITION
IS REALLY WEIGHING ON YOU ALL.

SO I WANTED TO DO
A ONE-ON-ONE WITH EVERYBODY.
SO LET'S START WITH XIOMARA.
Xiomara: WHAT'S UP?

YOU HAVE ANYTHING TO TELL ME
THAT I SHOULD--

Tyra: I DO, ACTUALLY.
Xiomara: LET'S TALK.

Tyra: I LOVE YOUR TOUGHNESS,
AND I FEEL LIKE YOU'RE TRYING

TO DO THIS FEMININE THING
THAT'S NOT NATURAL FOR YOU.
Xiomara: I WILL BE TOUGH.

Tyra: I JUST FEEL LIKE THAT
IS WHAT MAKES YOU SPECIAL.

Catie: I STILL NEED TO FIND
FIND COMFORT ZONE

WITH STILL BEING ME,
BUT NOT LOOKING LIKE PLAIN JANE.

Tyra: HOW ARE YOU HANDLING
YOUR STRESS AND PRESSURE?
Yoanna: BETTER. A LOT BETTER.
THE STRESS LEVEL IS NOT INTENSE.
I MEAN, I DO KINDA MISS MY MOM.

Tyra: MY MOM AND I
ARE LIKE THIS.
Yoanna: THAT'S LIKE MY MOM.

Tyra: MY MOM QUIT HER JOB
AND CAME WITH ME TO PARIS

WHEN I WAS 18,
AND SHE IS THE REASON WHY

I'M STANDING IN FRONT OF YOU
RIGHT HERE TODAY.
MY MOM IS MY ROCK.
Camille: OKAY.

THIS IS THE FIRST TIME
IN MY WHOLE ENTIRE LIFE
I HAVE EVER BEEN CALLED A DIVA.

Tyra: I SEE CAMILLE,
AND I SEE THE DIVA ATTITUDE.

THERE'S A CERTAIN LEVEL
OF HUMILITY, MODESTY
THAT YOU HAVE TO HAVE.

IT'S NOT ABOUT PROVING TO
THE WORLD HOW GREAT YOU CAN BE

WITH THIS THING ON YOUR CHEST
LIKE, "I'M GOOD, I'M GOOD,
I'M GOOD."
IT'S A QUIET CONFIDENCE.

April: I BELIEVE MY CALLING
IN LIFE IS TO BE A SOURCE

OF INSPIRATION AND STRENGTH
TO OTHER PEOPLE, BECAUSE THAT'S
WHEN I FEEL SO GOOD.

Tyra: I LOVE THAT YOU
SEE YOURSELF IN THAT WAY,
ESPECIALLY AS A WOMAN OF COLOR.
YOU KNOW?

April: I HAVEN'T
BEEN CONNECTED
WITH MY JAPANESE HERITAGE,

AND I'M NOT GONNA
PRETEND I HAVE.

SO I'M NOT TRYING TO MARKET
MYSELF TO JUST ASIAN GIRLS.

Sara: IT'S JUST,
I WANNA ASK YOUR OPINION ON WHAT

I SHOULD DO ABOUT MY DAD,
BECAUSE HE'S LEAVING MESSAGES

ON MY CELL PHONE RIGHT NOW
AND CALLING MY MOM.

Tyra: DOES HE KNOW
WHERE YOU ARE?

Sara: NO, HE DON'T.
Tyra: HE DOESN'T?

WOULD IT HELP YOU IN ANY WAY,
WOULD IT GIVE YOU STRENGTH
TO TALK TO HIM?

Sara: TO TALK TO HIM
JUST LIKE...

Tyra: WHETHER IT'S
A CURSE-OUT OR A...

Sara: IT WOULD BE OVER
IF I TALKED TO HIM RIGHT NOW.

Tyra: IT MIGHT BE SOMETHING
THAT YOU HAVE TO DEAL WITH.

MAYBE IN YOUR PHOTO SHOOTS
YOU ARE THINKING ABOUT HIM.

THERE'S AN ANGER,
BUT THERE'S MAYBE A SADNESS,

'CAUSE THAT'S WHAT I SEE
IN YOUR EYES WHEN YOU DO
PHOTO SHOOTS--IT'S A SADNESS.

Sara: REALLY?
Tyra: MM-HMM.
Sara: WOW.

Shandi: NOW I'M STARTING TO
SEE MORE, LIKE, SERIOUSLY,

I THINK I'VE GROWN MORE IN,
LIKE, THE PAST COUPLE OF WEEKS

THAN I HAVE GROWN, LIKE,
IN THE PAST COUPLE OF YEARS.

AND IF I GO BACK HOME
TO, LIKE, MY LIFE...

Tyra: I DON'T WANT YOU
TO GO BACK TO YOUR LIFE BEFORE,

GOING,
"THERE'S ALWAYS WALGREENS."

Shandi: YEAH, EVERYONE'S
LIKE, "NO MORE WALGREENS
FOR SHANDI."

Tyra: LOOK AT THAT
AS YOUR PAST AND LOOK

AT THIS WHOLE EXPERIENCE
AS BEING YOUR FUTURE.
Mercedes: OKAY.

Tyra: WELL, ONE THING
I WANNA TALK ABOUT WITH YOU

IS ON THE LAST PHOTO SHOOT,
I FELT LIKE YOU HAD
AN ATTITUDE WITH PEOPLE.
Mercedes: REALLY?

Tyra: YOU KNOW,
SO THAT'S JUST...

Mercedes: THAT SHOOT,
THAT DAY, I WASN'T FEELING WELL.

YOU THOUGHT I WAS GIVING
YOU ATTITUDE?

Tyra: NOT ME,
JUST IN GENERAL.

Mercedes: HAVING LUPUS--
I DON'T FEEL WELL,

AND I'M TRYING TO HIDE IT,
AND I'M TRYING TO BE STRONG.

Tyra: IF YOU GET ELIMINATED,
IT'S NOT GONNA BE BECAUSE

YOU'RE TIRED AT WORK,
BUT IF I THINK THAT YOU HAVE

AN ATTITUDE AND YOU DON'T WORK
WELL WITH OTHERS, I'M GONNA BE
LIKE, I DON'T KNOW ABOUT THAT.
YOU KNOW?
SO JUST BE HONEST AND SPEAK UP.
OKAY?

Mercedes: I FEEL MYSELF
JUST DRAINING DOWN,

BECAUSE I'M THINKING NEGATIVE,
I THINK I'M GONNA DIE.
I THINK MY LIVER'S GONNA GO OUT.
I'M HAVING SHORT TERM MEMORY.
MY HAIR IS FALLING OUT.
I FEEL VULNERABLE. I FEEL WEAK.
I'M HIDING ALL THESE THINGS.
I'M JUST TIRED OF IT.

SO WE WAKE UP, AND WE GO
TO, LIKE, LOWER EAST SIDE

TO MEET THIS GENTLEMAN
BY THE NAME

OF STAN CHRISTENSEN
AND LEARN ABOUT OUR PERSONALITY.
Stan: HI. I'M STAN.

WE'RE WORKING TO GET THESE GIRLS
FAMILIAR WITH WHAT IT IS

ABOUT THEMSELVES THAT
OTHER PEOPLE IDENTIFY WITH,

SO THEY CAN TALK ABOUT
THEMSELVES COMFORTABLY WHEN
THEY'RE IN INTERVIEW SITUATIONS.

WHAT I'M GOING TO INTRODUCE
TO YOU IS THE MAGIC OF CHARISMA,

HOW YOU CAN DRAW TO YOU
THE KIND OF ATTENTION

THAT MAKES YOU STAND OUT,
THAT MAKES PEOPLE LISTEN,

THAT MAKES PEOPLE NOTICE,
AND THAT'S PRETTY ESSENTIAL
TO A MODEL.

Sara: YOU KNOW,
MODELING IS A PACKAGE DEAL.

YOU HAVE TO LEARN HOW
TO WALK A RUNWAY

AND PORTRAY YOURSELF
IN A CERTAIN LIGHT.

Stan: WHAT WE'RE GONNA DO IS
GATHER SOME INFORMATION

ABOUT HOW EVERYBODY ELSE
PERCEIVES US.

Sara: WE ARE HANDED
SHEETS OF PAPER,

AND WE HAVE TO MARK OFF
ADJECTIVES THAT DESCRIBE

EACH ONE OF THE GIRLS,
AND HE'S GONNA HAND THEM

BACK TO THE GIRLS,
AND THEY GET TO SEE
WHAT WE SAID ABOUT THEM.
Xiomara: IT'S A LOT.

DO I HAVE TO SEE WHAT PEOPLE
THINK OF ME REALLY IN THE HOUSE?
"ADVENTUROUS, HEADSTRONG."

Yoanna: "STYLISH,
SOPHISTICATED."
Shandi: "QUIRKY, FRAGILE."

Catie: "SECRETIVE,
EMOTIONAL."

April: "RESPONSIBLE,
INTELLIGENT, SOPHISTICATED."
Sara: "KIND, EXOTIC."

Camille: "SUPERIOR,
RELENTLESS, HEADSTRONG, DEFIANT,

OUTSPOKEN, CUNNING, AGGRESSIVE,
OPINIONATED, DEMANDING
AND SINGLE-MINDED."
Stan: ANYBODY SURPRISED?
WHO FEELS ATTACKED?
OKAY.

Mercedes: CAMILLE WAS NOT
HAPPY WITH HER RESULTS.

SHE WAS, LIKE, SUCKING
HER LIPS AND ROLLING HER EYES.

Stan: CHARISMA IS ABOUT
THE WILLINGNESS TO DEAL

WITH PEOPLE'S JUDGMENTS,
OPINIONS AND CRITIQUES.

Camille: PEOPLE CAN SAY
WHAT THEY WANNA SAY,

THEY COULD FEEL
THE WAY THEY WANNA FEEL.

HONESTLY, LIKE, I COULDN'T
REALLY CARE LESS.
MY OBJECTIVE IS TO WIN.

Stan: THIS ONE'S
A LITTLE BIT MORE SERIOUS.

WE'RE GONNA DO A SERIES
OF EXERCISES IN WHICH

EACH OF YOU IS GONNA GET UP
AND TELL A LITTLE STORY

TO LET PEOPLE SEE
YOUR INDIVIDUALITY, WHO YOU ARE.

THE FIRST EXERCISE
GOES LIKE THIS.

"THERE'S SOMEONE IN THE WORLD
I LOVE, AND THE REASON
THAT I LOVE THEM IS..."
OKAY, COME ON UP.

Mercedes: OKAY, THE PERSON
WHO I LOVE MOST IS MY MOTHER,

BECAUSE I'VE BEEN THROUGH
SO MUCH WITH HER,
AND SHE LETS ME BE ME.

SHE LETS ME
BOUNCE OFF THE WALLS

AND BREAK DISHES, AND
SHE STILL LOVES ME

FOR WHO I AM, AND SHE JUST
MAKES ME FEEL GOOD INSIDE.

I'VE NEVER LIVED ON MY OWN
BEFORE, AND IT'S HARD,

BECAUSE I HAVEN'T BEEN
FEELING WELL, AND, YOU KNOW,
USUALLY MY MOM TAKES CARE OF ME.

Shandi: UM, I'VE GONE THROUGH
MY LIFE BEING, YOU KNOW,

THE BLACK SHEEP OF THE FAMILY
AND NOT HAVING ANYONE

TO TALK TO
OR EXPLAIN MY FEELINGS TO,

AND THE ONE PERSON THAT I LOVE
IN MY LIFE IS MY BOYFRIEND ERIC,

AND IT'S BECAUSE HE ACTUALLY
UNDERSTANDS ME MORE THAN ANYONE.

Xiomara: I CONSIDER SHANDI
MY FRIEND, AND I FEEL BAD,

BECAUSE SHE'S GOING THROUGH
A LOT RIGHT NOW.
Stan: THANK YOU VERY MUCH.

"THE WORST THING
I HAVE EVER DONE WAS..."

Sara: THE WORST THING
I HAVE EVER DONE IS PROBABLY

NOT BE HONEST WITH MY FATHER
MY ENTIRE LIFE JUST FOR THE FACT

THAT HE DOESN'T APPROVE OF
A LOT OF THE THINGS THAT I DO.

BUT MY MOTHER SUPPORTED ME 100%,
AND... (voice breaking)
I LOVE HER SO MUCH.

Catie: MY HEART ACHES
FOR SARA, BECAUSE HER FATHER

WILL DISOWN HER
WHEN HE FINDS OUT
SHE'S DOING THIS.

April: SARA HAD TO DEAL
WITH SOME NEGATIVITY

IN ASSOCIATION
WITH HER HERITAGE.
I HAVEN'T.
Sara: (laughs nervously)

Stan: THAT IS WHERE CHARISMA
COMES FROM.

IT COMES FROM
PUBLIC SELF-ACCEPTANCE.

THE MODELS THAT SUCCEED DO SO
NOT BECAUSE OF HOW THEY LOOK.

THEY DO IT BECAUSE THEY LET
PEOPLE SEE THEIR INDIVIDUALITY,
WHO THEY ARE.

Mercedes: IT WAS A GOOD WAY
TO GET TO KNOW

WHAT EVERYBODY REALLY THINKS,
BUT IT'S VERY DIFFICULT FOR ME

TO COME OUT
AND SHARE WHAT I'M FEELING.
Xiomara: (laughing)
Shandi: 28, 29...

Xiomara: PEOPLE ARE
TRYING TO SLEEP.

Mercedes: I'M FEELING BAD
AGAIN, AND I'M TIRED,

AND I'M JUST TRYING TO JUST,
LIKE, KEEP ON PUSHING MYSELF,

BECAUSE WHEN YOU HAVE LUPUS,
YOU CAN'T STRESS OUT,

AND IT'S DIFFICULT TO DO
IN THIS HOUSE, SO YOU KNOW,

I'M JUST TRYING TO STICK
IN THERE.

Shandi: MY MOM ALWAYS THOUGHT
THAT I LOOK LIKE A BOY.
Xiomara: NO, YOU DON'T.

Shandi: I WOULD, LIKE,
I USED TO WEAR, LIKE,

MY DAD'S, UM, ARMY PANTS,
BUT I, LIKE, CUT 'EM

AND MADE 'EM INTO SHORTS,
AND I WOULD COME HOME,

AND SHE'D BE LIKE,
"YOU WENT TO SCHOOL
LOOKING LIKE THAT?
YOU LOOK LIKE A... BUM."

MY MOM'S NOT HERE NOW,
SO I CAN JUST DO WHAT I WANT,

AND, YOU KNOW,
I DON'T HAVE ANYONE, YOU KNOW,
PUSHING ME DOWN ANYMORE.
Yoanna: HELLO, MR. ALEXANDER!

J.: WHAT'S GOING ON,
DARLING?
HEY.

Mercedes: J. ALEXANDER
IS THE RUNWAY DIVA.
HE TEACHES US HOW TO WALK.

Xiomara: AND HE'S COMING
OVER FOR DINNER, AND WE FIND OUT

THAT HE'S BRINGING
A SPECIAL GUEST.

J.: I'VE TRIED TO CALL HER,
BUT I DON'T KNOW WHERE SHE IS.
Yoanna: HI.
Mercedes: HELLO.
J.: HI, DARLIN'.
Suzannah: HI. HOW ARE YOU?
J.: HI, HONEY.
Catie: YOU'RE A PSYCHIC?
Suzannah: YES.
PSYCHIC INTUITIVE WORKS.
THIS WILL BE A LOT OF FUN.

Shandi: SUZE IS A PSYCHIC,
AND WE'RE GONNA GET
THIS PSYCHIC CONSULTATION.
Suzannah: THIS WILL BE FUN.
OKAY. I DON'T KNOW YOU.
I DON'T KNOW ANYTHING ABOUT YOU.
Catie: I DON'T KNOW.

DOESN'T IT MAKE THE DEVIL
COME OUT OR SOMETHING?

April: HALF OF THE GIRLS
ARE, LIKE, KINDA FLIPPING OUT.

Yoanna: DO YOU HAVE A GIFT,
OR ARE YOU...

Suzannah: I HAVE A GIFT,
AND I TAKE IT FROM YOU.

WHATEVER YOU COME IN WITH,
I READ YOU, SO LET'S GO.
YOUR DATE OF BIRTH?
Mercedes: 8/24/81.

Suzannah: MERCEDES,
YOUR BODY'S TIRED.
YOUR MIND ISN'T.

SOMETIMES YOU WANT TO DO
MORE THAN YOU PHYSICALLY CAN,
SO YOU'RE GONNA BE STRUGGLING.
DO YOU UNDERSTAND THAT?
Mercedes: I DON'T KNOW.

Suzannah: SOMETHING'S
BURDENING YOU.
I CAN SEE IT.

YOU DON'T KNOW?
Mercedes: MNH-MNH.
Suzannah: OKAY.

Mercedes: SHE'S DEAD ON,
AND SHE'S JUST DOING THIS

WITH NUMBERS, YOUR BIRTHDAY
AND YOUR NAME.

Suzannah: CAMILLE,
I'M JUST GONNA LEVEL WITH YOU,

AND I DON'T CARE
IF YOU PUNCH ME,
BUT YOU PUT PEOPLE OFF.

Camille: I'M NOT, LIKE,
BITING MY NAILS, LIKE,
"OH, MY GOD. NOBODY LIKES ME."

Sara: HOW DO YOU SEE
MY FATHER REACTING TO ME
BEING A MODEL?

Suzannah: HE'S GONNA HATE IT,
BUT HE'S GONNA SECRETLY LOVE IT.
Sara: REALLY?
Suzannah: MAKE PEACE WITH IT.
LET IT GO.
YOU'VE COME THIS FAR.

IF YOU HAVE THE COURAGE
TO DO THIS, BELIEVE ME,

YOU'D HAVE THE COURAGE
TO GO FURTHER.

Sara: SHE READ ME
LIKE A BOOK.
IT WAS REALLY ODD.

Suzannah: APRIL,
YOU ARE DETERMINED TO BE
A TOP MODEL NO MATTER WHAT.
YOU WILL BE A TOP MODEL.

XIOMARA, SOMETIMES, I THINK
IT'S EASY TO BE YOUR FRIEND,

BUT I DON'T KNOW HOW LONG
YOU REMAIN FRIENDS WITH PEOPLE.
IT ISN'T SHALLOW.

IT'S SELF-PROTECTION,
BUT THERE ARE

SOME VERY GENUINE PEOPLE
THAT WILL STAY FRIENDS WITH YOU.

OKAY, SHANDI, THERE'S A LOT
OF ADDICTIVE BEHAVIOR
IN YOUR FAMILY.
Shandi: MM-HMM.

Suzannah: SEE, I THINK
WHAT'S GOING ON WITH SHANDI
IS SHANDI NEEDS FAMILY.
DOES ANYBODY HUG YOU?
YOU DON'T GET HUGGED?

Shandi: WELL, I MEAN,
HERE, I DO.

Suzannah: YES,
YOU GET HUGGED.
Catie: WE LOVE SHANDI.
Xiomara: I LOVE SHANDI.

Suzannah: SEE--
EVERYBODY LOVES YOU.
SO YOU HAVE FAMILY.

EVEN IN THE MOMENT,
YOU HAVE FAMILY.
THAT MAKES YOU VERY RICH.

A LOT OF ISOLATED
AND LONELY SOULS.
IT'S OKAY, SHANDI.
Shandi: (crying)

Sara: SHANDI BREAKS MY HEART
BECAUSE HER PARENTS TREATED HER

LIKE THE BLACK SHEEP
OF THE FAMILY.
IT MAKES ME VERY ANGRY AT THEM.

J.: COME ON,
GIVE MAMA SOME SUGAR.

Shandi: I'M NOT CLOSE
WITH PRETTY MUCH
ANYONE IN MY FAMILY AT ALL.

I COULDN'T GO
GIVE THEM A HUG.

I COULDN'T SAY, YOU KNOW,
"I LOVE YOU. I MISS YOU."

AND IT'S JUST REALLY, REALLY
HARD TO DEAL WITH.
(continues crying)

Xiomara: EVEN THOUGH SHANDI'S MY
CLOSEST FRIEND IN THE HOUSE,

I NEVER KNEW HOW HORRIBLE
HER RELATIONSHIP SHE HAD

WITH HER PARENTS, AND,
YOU KNOW, THE LACK OF LOVE.
Catie: SO REMEMBER THIS--

GIRL, YOU HAVE NO IDEA HOW FAR
YOU CAN GO WITH YOUR LOOK.

April: YOU KNOW
HOW MANY PEOPLE SAID,

WHEN I TOLD THEM
I WAS TRYING OUT FOR THIS,
THE WORD "TOKEN ASIAN" TO ME?

Catie: BUT ACTUALLY,
THAT'S WHAT MAKES YOU STAND OUT.

April: EVEN MY MOM,
'CAUSE OBVIOUSLY,

SHE'S THE ONE WHO'S RESPONSIBLE
FOR ME BEING ASIAN--

SHE THINKS MODELS ARE
BIG-BOOBED, BLONDE-HAIRED

BARBIE DOLLS,
SO SHE DOESN'T LOOK AT ME

AND SEE A MODEL,
YOU KNOW WHAT I MEAN?
Catie: WHOO-HOO!
Stan: HEY.
Catie: HI, SAM!

Stan: THIS AFTERNOON,
A SURPRISE GUEST

IS GONNA INTERVIEW YOU
ONE BY ONE, AND YOU'RE GONNA DO

YOUR BEST TO USE
WHAT WE TALKED ABOUT YESTERDAY.

BE CHARISMATIC, BE COMFORTABLE,
BECAUSE WHOEVER DOES BEST

IS GONNA WIN A SHOPPING SPREE,
SO...
Woman: (gasps)

Xiomara: I HEAR "SHOPPING
SPREE," AND I'M LIKE,
"WHERE AND HOW MUCH?"

Stan: SO THE DETERMINATION
OF WHO WINS THAT SHOPPING SPREE
IS BASED ON BEING YOU, OKAY?
I'LL SEE YOU.

Mercedes: I CAN'T IMAGINE
WHO IT IS.
ARE WE GONNA MEET THE PRESS?
Xiomara: (laughing)
HEY, JANICE!

Janice: XIOMARA,
HOW YOU DOIN'?
YOU LOOK GOOD.
Xiomara: OH, GOD!

IT'S JANICE DICKINSON,
AND JANICE, YOU KNOW, LIKE,
TEARS YOU APART.

Janice: ARE YOU KIDDING ME
WITH THAT WALK?

YESTERDAY YOU WERE
TAUGHT HOW TO MAKE THE MOST
OUT OF YOUR PERSONALITY.

TODAY I'M GONNA ASK YOU
A FEW QUESTIONS

SO WE CAN GET TO KNOW
THE PERSONALITY INSIDE OF YOU.

WHAT'S THE CRAZIEST PLACE
YOU'VE EVER HAD SEX?

Xiomara: (laughing)
Janice: THE CRAZIEST.

Xiomara: UM,
IN A BROOM CLOSET
IN HIGH SCHOOL.

Camille: STUCK
IN A FERRIS WHEEL.
Catie: I'M A VIRGIN.

Janice: OKAY,
IF YOU COULD BE A JUDGE

AND ELIMINATE ANYONE,
WHO WOULD IT BE?

Camille: OOH,
THAT'S A HARD QUESTION.

Sara: RIGHT NOW
IT'D BE CAMILLE.

April: CAMILLE.
Xiomara: CAMILLE.

Yoanna: CAMILLE.
Janice: WHY?

Yoanna: BECAUSE
SHE'S A WITCH.

Janice: YOU SEEM TO BE
A LITTLE INTIMIDATED BY ME.
DO I MAKE YOU NERVOUS?
Camille: I LOVE YOU.

LIKE, PEOPLE MAY CALL YOU,
YOU KNOW, THE BITCH OR WHATEVER,

BUT IT'S JUST IN YOUR--
Janice: BITCH?

I DIDN'T SAY "BITCH,"
BUT ARE THEY CALLING ME A BITCH?

Camille: CERTAIN PEOPLE
MAY CALL YOU THAT.

Janice: YOU KNOW,
THAT WAS REALLY OFFENSIVE TO ME.

YOU KNOW, I'M A MEMBER
OF THE P.T.A.

SO, SARA, TELL ME WHY
YOU THINK YOU SHOULD WIN
THIS COMPETITION.

Sara: TO GIVE A GOOD IMAGE
OF MIDDLE EASTERN WOMEN.
SHE IS BEAUTIFUL. SHE'S EXOTIC.
SHE HAS AN OPINION.

SHE DOES NOT LET MEN
WALK ALL OVER HER.

Janice: I AM WOMAN.
Sara: I AM WOMAN.

Janice: THAT'S WHAT
YOU WANNA SAY.
Sara: YEAH.

Janice: SARA'S GOT
SO MUCH PERSONALITY,
AND SHE HAS SO MUCH DRIVE.
SHE SOLD ME.

APRIL, I'M GETTING A SENSE
THAT YOU'VE GOT THIS NEGATIVITY
TOWARDS YOUR ETHNICITY.

April: I'M HALF WHITE
AND HALF ASIAN, OKAY?

JUST BECAUSE I HAVEN'T
IDENTIFIED MYSELF AS AN ASIAN

OR AS A WHITE PERSON,
THAT DOESN'T MEAN
I'M REJECTING IT.

Janice: APRIL DOESN'T KNOW
WHAT TO CALL HERSELF,

SO THAT'S WHAT KINDA BOTHERS ME
ABOUT HER.

SHE CLEARLY LOOKS ASIAN,
AND SHE SHOULD BE PROUD OF IT.

IS THERE ANYTHING
THAT YOU'RE HIDING

THAT YOU'RE WORRIED
THAT WOULD COME OUT,
SHOULD YOU BECOME FAMOUS?
Shandi: PROBABLY THE DRUGS.

Janice: AND HOW DID YOU STOP,
OR HAVE YOU?

Shandi: I WAS, UM,
ARRESTED FOR, UM, ROBBERY,

AND I GOT ON PROBATION
FOR TWO YEARS.
I JUST LIKE BEING HONEST.

I'M NOT PRETENDING, "OH, YEAH,
I HAVEN'T DONE THIS.
I HAVEN'T DONE DRUGS."

IT'S LIKE A PART OF MY LIFE
THAT I WENT THROUGH,
AND IT'S, LIKE, IN MY PAST.

THE WHOLE TIME I'M DOING
ALL THESE STUPID DRUGS,

I WANTED MY PARENTS
